title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening the Work of Litigation Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Commercial Cases
keywords_en: Courts on strengthening foreign-related commercial cases
full_text_en:
Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Strengthening the Work of Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Commercial Cases

Fa [2004] No. 265

High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Since the implementation of the Interpretation No. 5 [2002] of the Supreme People's Court, the Provisions on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases, on March 1, 2002, courts at all levels have earnestly implemented it, established a new pattern for the adjudication of foreign-related commercial cases, improved the quality of adjudication and the competence of judges handling foreign-related commercial cases, and made significant contributions to meeting the challenges faced by China after its accession to the World Trade Organization. In order to further facilitate litigation for the parties, prevent the loss of foreign-related commercial cases, cultivate and make full use of judicial resources, and continuously enhance the capacity to adjudicate foreign-related commercial cases, it is hereby notified as follows in accordance with Article 1, paragraph (4) of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases:

1. For intermediate people's courts of appellate review that accept appeals in cases of border trade disputes, intermediate people's courts of appellate review for courts in economic and technological development zones established with the approval of the State Council, and other intermediate people's courts, if they need to be designated to have jurisdiction over first-instance foreign-related commercial cases, the high people's court of the locality shall submit a request to the Supreme People's Court for approval.

Each high people's court shall, on the basis of investigation, report to the Supreme People's Court by the end of March 2005 for designation the intermediate people's courts mentioned above that require such designation.

2. The high people's courts of Guangdong Province and the municipalities directly under the Central Government are authorized to designate, based on actual work needs, basic people's courts within their respective jurisdictions to have jurisdiction over first-instance foreign-related (including those involving Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan) commercial cases within their districts, clearly define the division of jurisdiction over cases between basic people's courts and intermediate people's courts, and report the circumstances of such designations to the Supreme People's Court for record.

3. Courts designated to have jurisdiction over first-instance foreign-related commercial cases must adhere to standards. Specialized foreign-related commercial adjudication tribunals or collegial panels shall be established, sufficient adjudication force shall be allocated, and the quality of adjudication shall be ensured. Where conditions are not yet met for having jurisdiction over first-instance foreign-related commercial cases, the training of judges shall be strengthened, and a request for designation may be submitted only after conditions are met.

4. Courts designated to have jurisdiction over first-instance foreign-related commercial cases shall promptly determine their jurisdictional areas and make them publicly known, so as to ensure the correct implementation of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Jurisdiction over Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Cases.

5. High people's courts shall effectively strengthen their supervision and guidance over the work of jurisdiction in foreign-related commercial cases, resolutely correct improper jurisdiction, earnestly resolve problems existing in the jurisdiction over foreign-related commercial cases, correctly exercise jurisdiction over foreign-related commercial cases, and safeguard the judicial authority of our country.

It is hereby notified.

December 29, 2004
